q: How much heat is needed to melt $0.20\,\text{kg}$ of ice at $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ ($s = 334\,\text{kJ/kg}$)?
a: $Q = sm = 334\,\tfrac{\text{kJ}}{\text{kg}} \cdot 0.20\,\text{kg} = 66.8\,\text{kJ} \approx 67\,\text{kJ}$. The temperature does not change during melting.

q: Mix $0.10\,\text{kg}$ of water ($10\,{}^\circ\text{C}$) and $0.10\,\text{kg}$ of ice ($0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$). Does all the ice melt? Justify with numbers.
a: No. As it cools to $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ the water can give out $Q = cm\Delta T = 4190\,\tfrac{\text{J}}{\text{kg}\cdot\text{K}} \cdot 0.10\,\text{kg} \cdot 10\,\text{K} \approx 4.2\,\text{kJ}$, but melting all the ice needs $sm = 334\,\tfrac{\text{kJ}}{\text{kg}} \cdot 0.10\,\text{kg} = 33.4\,\text{kJ}$. Only about $12.5\,\text{g}$ melts, and the temperature is $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$.
